column1: # mapping_set_title: CIAAW draft vocabulary - alignment with OBO ontologies, the SI Digital Framework, Wikidata and earlier terms
#   How the classes and properties of model/ontology.ttl relate to BFO, IAO, OBI and ChEBI, to the SI Reference
#   Point of the SI Digital Framework, to the classes and properties of Wikidata, and to the Chemrof and QUDT terms
#   this prototype used before. Nothing is
#   imported: the mappings say where each term would go for someone who aligns the data with those ontologies.
#   The mappings of single elements and isotopes to ChEBI and Wikidata are in data/ciaaw.sssom.tsv.

column7: comment
Each element stands for a subclass of atom in ChEBI, such as hydrogen atom. The element individuals are mapped to those classes in data/ciaaw.sssom.tsv.
The class this prototype used before. Replaced because Chemrof is young and its terms still change.
Each isotope stands for a class of atoms with one mass number in ChEBI, such as protium. ChEBI has no class for isotopes in general.
The class this prototype used before.
A declaration is information about an element or isotope: what CIAAW recommended, not a property of a material. IAO places information content entities under BFO generically dependent continuant.
Same pattern as the SI Reference Point: a stable resource with versioned definitions.
The object is an element or isotope, which stands for a kind of atom (see ciaaw:ChemicalElement). In OWL with IAO this becomes: the declaration is about some atom of that class.
IAO uses it for measurement data. A declaration is a recommended value, not a measurement.

Wikidata gives the atomic weight of an element as its mass in dalton. check_wikidata_weights.py compares the two.
